title: Goalkeeper Basics
description: Learn the keeper habits that help the whole team stay calm and organized.

questions.question: What is a useful ready position before a shot?
options: Balanced, knees slightly bent, hands ready
Leaning all your weight onto one leg
Standing stiffly with feet together
Still taking large steps as the shot comes
questions.explanation: A balanced position helps you react in either direction. Stay ready to move rather than locking your legs.

questions.question: When should a goalkeeper try to get set for a shot?
options: Just before the shooter strikes
Only after seeing which corner the shot targets
As soon as play enters the half, without moving again
Only after the ball bounces
questions.explanation: Adjust your position as the attack develops, then aim to be balanced when the ball is struck.

questions.question: You save a shot but the ball stays loose. What next?
options: Recover your position and watch for the next shot
Turn to check the goal net first
Start moving upfield for a pass
Assume a defender will collect it
questions.explanation: Stay involved after the first save. A loose ball may create another chance, so recover and communicate.

questions.question: A shot comes straight at you. What is usually safest?
options: Hold it securely if possible, otherwise direct it away from danger
Push every shot straight ahead
Try to catch every shot even when off balance
Kick at every shot instead of using your hands
questions.explanation: Choose the action you can control. A secure catch removes the rebound; a controlled deflection can help when catching is not realistic.

questions.question: In which area may a goalkeeper normally use their hands?
options: Their own penalty area
Anywhere in their own half
Either penalty area
Only their own goal area, the smaller box
questions.explanation: The ball must be in the keeper's own penalty area. Some situations still forbid handling, including a deliberate kick to the keeper by a teammate.

questions.question: A teammate deliberately kicks the ball to you as goalkeeper. How should you play it?
options: Use your feet, not pick it up
Pick it up as long as it is in your penalty area
Pick it up only if a forward is pressing
Let it roll toward goal without reacting
questions.explanation: Under the standard Laws, you cannot handle a ball deliberately kicked to you by a teammate. Control or pass with your feet.

questions.question: Why are clear goalkeeper calls useful?
options: They help defenders spot danger and organize
They replace the need to adjust your position
They mean defenders no longer need to look around
They let every defender chase the ball
questions.explanation: Use short, useful information. Tell teammates about runners, pressure, or a ball you are coming to claim.

questions.question: You commit to safely catching a cross. Which call is clearest?
options: Keeper!
Someone get it!
Maybe mine!
Over there!
questions.explanation: An early, clear call tells teammates your decision. They still need to watch opponents and avoid unfairly blocking them.

questions.question: A cross is beyond your reach in a crowd. What is a sensible decision?
options: Let defenders challenge, then adjust and get ready for the next ball
Charge through the crowd regardless
Stop moving because you cannot catch it
Follow the ball so far that you lose sight of goal
questions.explanation: Judge the flight, distance, and traffic. If you cannot claim safely, stay involved and prepare for a shot or second ball.

questions.question: A forward breaks through. You cannot reach the ball first. How can you help?
options: Adjust your distance, stay balanced, and make the shooting angle smaller
Sprint past the ball carrier
Dive at their feet from too far away
Keep moving forward even when they are about to shoot
questions.explanation: You may delay the shot and allow defenders to recover. Get balanced as the attacker prepares to finish; avoid a reckless challenge.

questions.question: A shooter moves wide. How should a keeper adjust?
options: Move with the shooting angle while covering the near side and the rest of goal
Stay in the exact center regardless
Stand touching the near post regardless of distance
Turn fully toward the far post
questions.explanation: Position relative to the ball and goal. Protecting the near side does not mean leaving the rest of the goal unguarded.

questions.question: After a secure catch, what should you do?
options: Scan quickly and choose a useful distribution
Throw to the first shirt you see
Wait until every teammate is marked
Always punt before looking
questions.explanation: Look for a realistic way to start the attack and release within the allowed time. The best option can be short or long.

questions.question: In the diagram, A is open nearby with a clear passing lane. What is a sensible option?
questions.imageAlt: Goalkeeper distribution options with a short open teammate
options: Roll or pass to A
Kick into the nearest opponent
Wait for A to be marked
Dribble into the pressure ahead
questions.explanation: A short open option can help keep possession. Check the lane and A's readiness before releasing the ball.

questions.question: Short options are tightly marked and pressure is close. What may be sensible?
options: A longer clearance toward a safer area
A short pass through the closest opponent
Holding the ball beyond the allowed time
Dribbling across your goal regardless of pressure
questions.explanation: Protect the goal first. A longer ball can relieve pressure when short passes are unsafe.

questions.question: Before a corner is taken, what helps the goalkeeper?
options: Check the position of runners and teammates and give clear calls
Watch only the kicker and ignore the box
Wait until the ball arrives to organize
Stand behind the goal line for more space
questions.explanation: Prepare before the delivery. Know who is covering key spaces, then react to the flight of the ball.

questions.question: A hard shot cannot be caught securely. Where should you try to direct it?
options: Away from waiting attackers, often toward a wide area
Back toward the penalty spot regardless
Toward the nearest attacker to make them move
Directly in front of your goal whenever possible
questions.explanation: Try to make a follow-up finish harder. The safest direction depends on where attackers and teammates are.

questions.question: Your goalkeeper has the ball. How can outfield players help?
options: Show at different safe passing angles
All stand directly in front of the keeper
Stay behind opponents and ask for a pass
Run forward without checking the keeper
questions.explanation: Make it possible to pass to you. Check pressure and leave useful distances between teammates.

questions.question: What does being brave and sensible as a goalkeeper mean?
options: Commit to a decision you can carry out safely
Dive into every challenge regardless of who gets there first
Never leave the goal line
Take a risky option to look confident
questions.explanation: Confidence includes knowing when to act and when to stay ready. Safety and control matter more than making a dramatic save.

questions.question: A through ball is rolling toward the edge of your area. What should guide whether you come out?
options: The ball's speed, your distance, the runner, and where you can reach it
Only whether the crowd shouts
Only whether it is on your stronger-foot side
Whether you came out for the previous pass
questions.explanation: Read each situation again. Outside the penalty area, you must play without your hands and avoid dangerous contact.

questions.question: What is a goalkeeper's main role?
options: Protect the goal and help organize the team
Only kick the ball long
Stay in one position regardless of play
Leave all passing decisions to defenders
questions.explanation: Keepers save shots, communicate, and help their team keep or regain control of the ball.

questions.question: Your team keeps a high defensive line. What should affect how far you stand off your goal line?
options: The ball, pressure on the passer, runners, and your recovery distance
Only the position you used for the last attack
Only how far forward your center-backs ask you to stand
Only whether your team is winning
questions.explanation: A supporting keeper can deal with through balls, but must also protect against a shot over them. Adjust as pressure and space change.

questions.question: A pass back draws a forward toward you. A defender is now open on the other side. What may the keeper's next pass achieve?
options: Move the ball away from the press through the newly opened lane
Keep the forward close by taking extra touches
Return to the same crowded side to avoid changing direction
Send the ball long without checking the open defender
questions.explanation: The keeper can help move the press, not just receive a rescue pass. Scan before the ball arrives and release with suitable pace.

questions.question: You dive and push a shot wide. The ball stays in play and an attacker approaches it. What is the next priority?
options: Recover toward the new shooting angle while watching the ball
Return to the exact middle regardless of where the ball is
Watch the previous shot path while staying on the ground
Leave the goal to argue about the first shot
questions.explanation: The danger has moved. Recover quickly, locate the ball, and prepare for a follow-up from its new position.

questions.question: A teammate takes a throw-in directly to you inside your penalty area. Under standard Laws, how should you play it?
options: Use your feet without picking it up
Catch it because a throw is different from a kick
Catch it only if you stay inside the goal area
Catch it after it bounces once
questions.explanation: A goalkeeper may not handle a ball received directly from a teammate's throw-in. Plan a safe next pass with the feet before it arrives.

questions.question: You are ready to distribute after a catch. A distant winger has space, but a nearby defender is tightly marked. What should guide the choice?
options: Whether the throw or kick can reach the open winger safely
The nearby option must be safer because it is shorter
Long distribution is only useful after a goal kick
The closest player should decide without you scanning
questions.explanation: Shorter is not automatically safer. Compare the passing route, distance, and receiver's situation before choosing.
